claim: Dead workers no longer leak suite children: (1) the runner reaps its whole descendant tree on every exit path — normal, wall, RSS cap, host floor, directive kill — via `managent treekill` (a ps-table descendant walk with a last-poll seed for reparented/nested-session members), and its normal-exit path can no longer hang on a leaked grandchild that inherited the runner's pipes (the drain is now time-bounded, so the C2 reap runs and kills the pipe-holder); (2) `tools/runner --reap-orphans` ships the sweeper for pre-existing orphans: it matches only `.zig-cache/o/<hash>/test` suite binaries, skips any candidate whose live ancestry contains a worker marker (`subagent` / `claude -p` / `runner` / `fleet-keeper`) OR any live non-zig session ancestor (console/terminal/interactive shell — the hardening that keeps it from killing live work), and kills only candidates seen orphaned on two passes ≥45 s apart, logging every reap with pid, RSS and the reason. Controls: tools/regression-runner-reap.sh (9 arms, all green, wired into `zig build test`).

design.the_briefs_red_is_historical: The brief (2026-08-20) says the runner 'kills a process group yet zig build's children survive' and demands the first control FAIL against current code. Between the brief and this task, T557 (pass-1 process ownership, 2026-08-21) replaced the pgid kill with `managent treekill` and cannibalized the runner to call it on every exit path (C1 kill paths, C2 normal exit, C3 exception). So the runner side of the brief was already built; T548's regression suite now locks it in and quotes the red as history. The brief's 'establish which' (do suite children escape the group via setsid, or does the build daemon outlive the signal?) is answered structurally: the fix kills the whole descendant tree enumerated from the process table (plus a last-poll seed for members reparented to init), so it covers both escape mechanisms — the A1 control exercises the setsid-escapee shape explicitly.
design.new_defect_found_drain_hang: The normal-exit path had a blocking read of the child's remaining stderr/stdout after the child exited (`_drain_stderr`/`_drain_stdout` set the fd blocking and called `read()`). A leaked grandchild that INHERITED the runner's pipes — exactly the T548 leak shape, `zig build`'s test binaries holding the build pipe — keeps the write end open, so the read waits forever: the runner never exits, the C2 reap never runs, and the leaked memory is held indefinitely (and the worker row hangs). Reproduced red: the A3 fixture (child inherits the runner's pipes, holder exits after 12 s) hung the runner past 240 s with a launch-only run record. Fixed: `_drain_stream` reads non-blockingly with a 2 s deadline (normal case reads everything at EOF instantly; the leak case proceeds to the C2 reap, which kills the pipe-holder and closes the pipe). Green: the same fixture exits 0 in 3.5 s with `treekill ... claimed=1 killed=1 survivors=0`.
design.sweeper: `tools/runner --reap-orphans` — standalone host-level mode (no repo needed; timer/keeper-friendly), mirroring the existing `--sweep`. One pass: snapshot `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,rss=,state=,lstart=,command=`; match candidates with `\.zig-cache/o/<hash>/test`; walk each candidate's LIVE ancestry: skip on a worker marker, skip on a live non-zig session ancestor, orphan only when the chain reaches init (pid 1) through zig-build processes; then kill candidates seen orphaned on a previous pass ≥`--orphan-pass-min` (default 45 s) ago. State persists in /tmp/weizigo/runner-orphan-sweep.json (atomic tmp+rename; `--orphan-state-file` overrides for tests; the lstart field guards against pid reuse). Every reap is logged with pid, RSS and the reason on stderr AND appended to /tmp/weizigo/orphan-reap.log (silent process killing is unauditable). `--orphan-dry-run` reports without killing. Exit 0 always: a sweep is report + reap, never a gate. stdout carries one parseable summary line (`orphan-sweep: candidates=N reaped=M tracked=K mode=...`); stderr carries the per-process diagnostics.
design.guard_hardening_live_session: The brief's guard (b) list (subagent / claude -p / runner / fleet-keeper) is the literal minimum; on 2026-08-22 this host had THREE live `.zig-cache/o/*/test` binaries with NO worker marker in their chain: a `nohup zig build test` launched from a closed task (chain ends at a bash whose ppid is 1) and a `pi` console chain. The literal guard set would have classified all three as orphans and reaped live work after two passes. The sweeper therefore adds: skip any candidate whose live ancestry contains a live NON-ZIG process (console, terminal, interactive shell) — only chains that reach init through zig-build processes and dead pids are orphans. Verified against the live host: all three real suite binaries classified skip; a dry-run sweep reported candidates=0. The seat's own warning is the justification: 'a reaper that kills live work is far worse than the leak.'
design.two_pass_guard: A candidate must be seen orphaned on two runs ≥45 s apart (pass 1 records first_seen in the state file; pass 2 reaps). This protects a freshly spawned test whose parent link is not yet visible in a ps snapshot (transient race — the walk dead-ends at a missing ppid and skips that pass, and the 45 s second observation confirms it is genuinely abandoned). `--orphan-pass-min` is injectable so the regression suite exercises the mechanism in seconds, never minutes.

bars.A1_worker_killed_both_children: PASS — a stub worker spawns a long-lived child AND a setsid-escapee child (the pgid-kill hole), then is killed by the RSS cap: exit 124, treekill survivors=0, both children dead. RED against the 2026-08-20 killpg code (the escapee survived — that was the 9.1 GB leak); GREEN today via the tree-walk reap.
bars.A2a_wall: PASS — silent worker with a long-lived child under --max-wall 3 --progress-timeout 0: wall ceiling fires, exit 124, survivors=0, child dead.
bars.A2b_rss_cap: PASS — worker with a long-lived child under --rss-cap-mb 50: RSS cap fires, exit 124, survivors=0, child dead.
bars.A2c_host_floor: PASS — worker with a long-lived child under an INJECTED WEIZIGO_HOST_MEM_AVAIL_MB=100 reading (floor derived from hw.memsize ≈ 6144 MB; the host is never exhausted to test this): host guard fires, exit 124, survivors=0, child dead.
bars.A2d_directive: PASS — worker with a long-lived child under a scratch-repo runner; a kill directive written to the scratch directives.jsonl mid-run: 'directive D548 KILL' fires, exit 124, survivors=0, child dead.
bars.A3_null_live_work: PASS — a LIVE runner-owned suite-shaped child survives two sweeps (worker-marker guard) and is then reaped by the runner's NORMAL exit (C2) even though it inherited the runner's pipes (the drain-hang regression: under the pre-fix runner this arm hung forever).
bars.A4_sweeper_orphan_only: PASS — a pre-existing orphan (reparented to launchd) and a live runner-owned child side by side: pass 1 tracks the orphan without reaping (two-pass guard), pass 2 reaps the orphan only; the live child is untouched.
bars.A5_one_pass_never: PASS — an orphan seen for ONE pass only is never reaped: two passes with fresh state files each reaped nothing; the second observation ≥1 s apart (injected --orphan-pass-min 1) reaped it.
bars.A6_live_session: PASS — an orphan-SHAPED suite binary attached to a LIVE non-worker session (a console/shell stand-in) survives two sweeps: the live-session hardening protects the `pi`-console and nohup-terminal shapes the literal guard list misses.
bars.isolation: PASS — the whole suite runs from a scratch git repo under /tmp/weizigo; the closing F3 check confirms no fixture heartbeat line reached the LIVE heartbeat.jsonl.
bars.existing_suites: PASS — tools/regression-runner-reporting.sh and tools/regression-runner-guard.sh (both wired into zig build test) still pass after the drain change; `zig build` compiles the build.zig wiring.

files_integration_deferred.none: The sweeper mode and the regression are both in the committed deliverables. The timer/keeper hook (running `tools/runner --reap-orphans` periodically) is NOT wired anywhere yet — the brief says it 'belongs on a timer or in the keeper's loop' and names no deliverable for that; tools/fleet-keeper.sh is held by T511 (dispatchable) and was left untouched. The hook point is documented in the runner docstring; a one-line `tools/runner --reap-orphans` in a cron or the keeper's loop activates it.

run.summary: All 9 arms PASS: A1 (worker killed; child + setsid-escapee reaped, survivors=0), A2a wall, A2b RSS cap, A2c host floor (injected), A2d directive kill — each exit path reaps with treekill survivors=0; A3 live worker's child untouched by sweeps then reaped on normal exit (the drain-hang regression); A4 sweeper takes the pre-existing orphan only; A5 one-pass orphan never reaped; A6 session-attached child never reaped. F3 isolation: no fixture heartbeat in the live log. Existing runner suites (runner-reporting, runner-guard) still green; zig build compiles.
run.live_host_sweep: A dry-run `--reap-orphans` against the live host reported candidates=0 while three real `.zig-cache/o/*/test` suite binaries were running — all three classified skip via the live-session guard (one `nohup zig build test` chain under ppid 1, two `pi` console chains). The sweeper does not brake the live fleet.
